proof: Alt+G and the real date dialog load old revealed data through actual bounded history HTTP. No response substitution.
Modeled clock, track source sequences, full portfolio and ledger remain equal across date navigation and chart layout/period/link changes. No order placement is part of this qualification.
An unlinked 1m sibling retains its viewport. Linked 5m/1m charts locate one time; the 1m chart replaces a full 10000-row display window with a bounded old-date window.
The same revealed boundary and fixed input epochs travel in history requests/replies. A future date issues no history read and cannot advance the run.
Complete normal quit/restart retains the authoritative clock and portfolio; view-only date navigation continues. A separate HIDE_ALL training has no absolute date button or Alt+G dialog.

regressions.fullWindow: Actual fail-before/pass-after test: overlapping date history could evict its own requested candle when a full display store retained the newest rows. Date reads now own a bounded replacement window, leaving the execution store intact and the normal right-edge restore available.
regressions.runWorkspaceScope: Earlier native package registered date navigators under a bare workspace ID while the coordinator used replay:run:workspace. It showed unavailable without issuing the target read; current production binding matches the run/workspace scope.
regressions.staticCssImport: An initial complete check failed the real replay hub test module on a static CSS import. The date dialog is loaded lazily like existing replay dialogs; final complete check passes.
regressions.harness: Preserved failures include a target already loaded in the initial 12h fixture, clicking a clipped pinned period instead of the visible compact picker, datetime-local :00 normalization, reading snapshot instead of command output for a viewport, and checking native paint before the next frame. Final script uses real picker/input/output and waits for observed viewport coverage; no forced click or readiness bypass.
regressions.fixtureReuse: Final successful flow resumes the stopped owned 15000-row fixture/run after saved harness failures, closes its extra visible chart through the normal workspace action, then re-creates the test split. Original source/profile retained; each preparation advance occurs before the financial baseline is captured. No default-user profile launch.
